hints: Focus on the two things that control gas volume here, the balanced decomposition equation and how many moles you get from the same mass.
Write out the four decompositions and notice that each carbonate gives 1 mole of gas per mole of solid, while each nitrate gives 2.5 moles of gas per mole of solid.
Combine that gas ratio with moles equals mass divided by Mr, so for equal mass the compound with more gas per mole and a smaller Mr will win.
walkthrough:
**Write the decomposition equations**

Think of it simply, carbonates release only carbon dioxide, nitrates release nitrogen dioxide plus oxygen.

$$\text{CaCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$\text{BaCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{BaO} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$2\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CaO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$
$$2\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{BaO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Count gas moles per mole of solid**

This is the key difference. Each carbonate makes 1 mole of gas, each nitrate makes 2.5 moles of gas.

$$1 \text{ mol carbonate} \rightarrow 1 \text{ mol gas}$$
$$1 \text{ mol nitrate} \rightarrow 2.5 \text{ mol gas}$$

**Account for equal mass using Mr**

Equal mass does not mean equal moles. Moles equals mass divided by Mr, so a lighter compound gives more starting moles.

$$n = \frac{m}{M_r}$$
$$M_r(\text{CaCO}_3) \approx 100, \quad M_r(\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2) \approx 164$$
$$M_r(\text{BaCO}_3) \approx 197, \quad M_r(\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2) \approx 261$$

**Combine both effects**

Gas per gram equals (gas per mole) divided by Mr. Calcium nitrate has the winning combination of high gas per mole and low Mr for a nitrate.

$$\text{CaCO}_3: \frac{1}{100} = 0.0100$$
$$\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2: \frac{2.5}{164} \approx 0.0152$$
$$\text{BaCO}_3: \frac{1}{197} \approx 0.0051$$
$$\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2: \frac{2.5}{261} \approx 0.0096$$
The largest value gives the greatest volume under the same conditions.

options.A: CaCO3 gives only 1 mole of $\text{CO}_2$ per mole and has $M_r \approx 100$. Although it has the smallest Mr, its gas per mole is much lower than the nitrates, so its gas per gram (0.0100) is less than calcium nitrate.
options.B: Ca(NO3)2 decomposes to give 2.5 moles of gas per mole: $2\text{NO}_2 + 0.5\text{O}_2$. With a moderate $M_r \approx 164$, its moles of gas per gram, $2.5/164$, is the highest of the four, so it gives the greatest gas volume for equal mass.
options.C: BaCO3 gives only 1 mole of $\text{CO}_2$ per mole and has a large $M_r \approx 197$. It therefore has both a low gas ratio and few moles in the same mass, giving the smallest gas volume.
options.D: Ba(NO3)2 does give 2.5 moles of gas per mole, but its $M_r \approx 261$ is the largest. Equal mass therefore contains the fewest moles among the nitrates, so its gas per gram (0.0096) is beaten by the calcium nitrate.
